clue.text: Prank caught by a tourist worker in turn

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in turn says the worker's title is read the other way round

parts.note: a rep is a holiday company's representative looking after tourists

explanation.surface: A holiday rep pulls a practical joke and is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep is a travel company's representative who looks after holidaymakers at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful trick or escapade, the same as a prank.

clue.text: Terrible tone set by politician in court giving offence there?

indicators.note: in says the mixed letters and politician sit inside the court
terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An awful tone adopted by an MP in court causes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to the court: contempt of court is the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is disrespect or disobedience towards a judge, a punishable offence.

clue.text: Normal bargain for root vegetable

parts.note: par means the normal level
a snip is a bargain in British slang

explanation.surface: An ordinary deal on a root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a pale tapering root eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Study audition of hell-raising actor

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the actor's name is heard as a sound-alike

parts.note: Oliver Reed was a famously hard-drinking, hell-raising actor

explanation.surface: Look into the audition of a wild actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a casting session but means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is to study it, especially at a British university.

clue.text: City director firstly entertained by, maybe, a natural raconteur's device

indicators.note: entertained by says the city and the director's initial are held as guests inside the other piece

parts.note: a natural is a musical note, so 'maybe a natural' is A NOTE
EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: firstly says only the opening letter of director is used

explanation.surface: A City boss is entertained by someone gifted at telling stories.
explanation.walkthrough: A natural in music is a note, hence 'maybe'. ECD goes inside A NOTE, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing story, the stock-in-trade of a teller of tales.

clue.text: Revised modern reading inspires international bestselling author

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, so the rearranged letters take in the I
revised means reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An updated modern reading inspires a world-famous writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine Gordimer was a Nobel-winning South African novelist whose books sold widely.

clue.text: Reticent type turns up in abnormal clothing

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words abnormal clothing, across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shy person appears in strange clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked the hiding signal: 'in' marks the letters tucked inside 'abnormal clothing', and in a down clue 'turns up' reads them bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is to go silent, so a clam is a byword for someone who keeps quiet.

clue.text: Show more dishonesty adopting new statement lacking details

indicators.note: adopting says the letter is taken in by the first word

parts.note: to outlie is to lie more than someone else

explanation.surface: Being more dishonest by taking up a new statement short on detail.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a summary giving the main points without the particulars.

clue.text: Military hero leads to lively celebrations in festival

indicators.note: in says those letters go inside the festival

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

indicators.note: leads to says the opening letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: A war hero brings on lively celebrations at a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid was the eleventh-century Castilian warrior celebrated in Spanish epic.

clue.text: Flags could be required for this creative type?

definitions.text: Flags could be required for this creative type?

parts.words: Flags could be required for this creative type?
parts.note: flags here are flagstones, the slabs a street chalk artist draws on, not banners

explanation.walkthrough: Flags suggests banners, but flagstones are the paving slabs this artist decorates.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavement artist draws chalk pictures on the paving for passers-by.

clue.text: Northern country includes very advanced, idyllic state

indicators.note: includes says the country holds the letter for very inside it

parts.note: Iran is a country
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level

explanation.surface: A northern nation contains a very developed, perfect way of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect bliss or peace, an ideal condition.

clue.text: Radical dictators take to posturing

indicators.note: take means remove, so the letters of the word 'to' come out of the fodder
posturing suggests striking poses, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Extreme dictators like to strike poses.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and O from DICTATORS, leaving DICTARS, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme or far-reaching ones, the same as radical measures.

clue.text: Heroines oddly ignored for long periods

indicators.note: oddly ignored says the odd-placed letters are dropped and the even ones kept

explanation.surface: Heroic women are strangely overlooked for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are vast spans of time, ages beyond counting.

clue.text: Casually agreed about eating crusts of overgrown bloomer

indicators.note: eating says the reversed yes swallows the crust letters
about says the casual yes is turned round

parts.note: yep is a casual yes

indicators.note: crusts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of overgrown

explanation.surface: Someone casually agrees about eating the crusts of an overgrown loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a loaf of bread, a British crusty bloomer, but here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and the peony is a showy flowering shrub.

clue.text: Gloss over one-time trading association, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than seen, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a guild was a medieval association of merchants or craftsmen

explanation.surface: A historic trade body hides its faults.
explanation.definitionFit: To gild is to cover with a thin gold layer, so to give a deceptively fine surface.

clue.text: Haggard female in family after end to partying

indicators.note: after says the female relative comes after that letter
end to says the last letter of partying

parts.note: an aunt is a female relative

explanation.surface: A worn-out female relative after the party ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt describes a person thin and drawn from hardship or illness, a synonym of haggard.

clue.text: Medical officer in hearing given to making cracks?

indicators.note: in hearing says the name is heard as a sound-alike

parts.note: Chris Whitty was England's Chief Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A doctor giving evidence at a hearing is prone to cracking jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Whitty was England's Chief Medical Officer during the Covid pandemic; 'cracks' here are wisecracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty person is quick with clever jokes or wisecracks.

clue.text: A wee pun again devised to encapsulate timeless place in country

indicators.note: to encapsulate says the rearranged letters wrap round the trimmed word
devised means freshly put together, so the letters are rearranged
timeless says T, the abbreviation for time, is dropped

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A small joke repeated is invented to capture an eternal spot in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place in' reads like a location; 'in' is only a link, and 'place' is the verb put.
explanation.definitionFit: Papua New Guinea is a nation occupying the eastern half of New Guinea island.

clue.text: Rarefied ground or site retained by English clubs

indicators.note: retained by says the rearranged letters are held between the two abbreviations

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclusive golf course or venue kept by English clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground or site' suggests a venue; 'ground' is really the anagram signal, giving SOTERI between E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select few, refined beyond common reach.

clue.text: Familiar airs unsettled saturnine guest

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Well-known songs upset a gloomy visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Signature tunes are the recognisable melodies that announce a programme or performer.

clue.text: Provisional line essentially followed by first person in style

indicators.note: followed by says the next part comes after
essentially says the central letters of line, its essence
in says the pronoun sits inside the word for style

parts.note: a term is a name or style
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A temporary line is followed by the first person dressed stylishly.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is a temporary one lasting until something permanent is in place.

clue.text: Figure left after period linked to fossil fuel?

parts.note: NUM, the National Union of Mineworkers, is the coal miners' union

indicators.note: after says the letter for left comes behind the word for period

parts.note: an era is a period

explanation.surface: A number left after an era tied to coal.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM was the British coal miners' trade union, so it is linked to fossil fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a written symbol for a number, such as a digit.

clue.text: Get too old for romantic meeting

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an outing with a sweetheart

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate meanings of one word, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Styles date when they become outmoded, and a date is also an arranged romantic engagement.

clue.text: Dissent on the rise picked up by hearsay? Not relating to us

indicators.note: on the rise says the letters read upwards, reversed in this down clue
relating to us is our, so those letters are removed

parts.note: something rumoured is heard by hearsay

explanation.surface: Dissent spreading through rumour that doesn't concern us.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMOURED without OUR is RUMED, which reads upward to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection, or as a noun an expression of doubt.

clue.text: Artist cuts offer for thread

indicators.note: cuts says the artist slices into the offer

parts.note: a bid is an offer
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter slashes an offer for a strand.
explanation.definitionFit: To braid is to interlace strands, and as a noun braid is a woven thread or trim.

clue.text: Section of network's muting mildly offensive comments

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a broadcaster's muting covers lightly rude remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or bawdy talk, often of the mild, smirking kind.

clue.text: Favour element disowning Republican

indicators.note: disowning says the Republican letter is cast out

parts.note: boron is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A favour given by a component rejecting a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something granted as a kindness.

clue.text: Large-scale Eastern film

parts.note: a pic is a film, short for picture

explanation.surface: A grand film from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one film; the adjective alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic means vast in scope or size, heroic in scale.

clue.text: Inventive sort taking round at home ordinary stuff

parts.note: marc is the stuff left after pressing grapes

indicators.note: round says the word for at home is turned the other way

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A creative person takes a lap of the house with everyday things.
explanation.walkthrough: Marc is the pulpy residue left after pressing grapes, used for brandy; 'stuff' as a noun means material.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the inventor who pioneered radio telegraphy.

clue.text: Rare poem composed but without a commanding figure?

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are rearranged
without says the letter A is left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: An unusual poem is written but lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of RARE POEM, leaving RREPOEM, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler, someone who commands an empire.

clue.text: Consider minutes taken in abandoned building at rear of office

indicators.note: taken in says the minutes go inside the ruin

parts.note: a ruin is a derelict building

indicators.note: rear of says the last letter of office

explanation.surface: Think about the minutes found in a derelict building behind the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder deeply, chewing over a thought.

clue.text: Kiwi dancer shortly in charge gets abdominal pain

indicators.note: shortly says the surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Brendan Cole is a New Zealand ballroom dancer, a former Strictly Come Dancing professional

explanation.surface: A New Zealand dancer soon takes charge and gets a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi is slang for a New Zealander; Brendan Cole was a professional on BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe spasmodic pain in the belly, common in babies.
